corrected_content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $A(4,-3,\sqrt{2})$ and is parallel to the vectors ${\mathbf{v}}_{\mathbf{1}}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}$ and ${\mathbf{v}}_{\mathbf{2}}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.$.
corrected_content.worked_solution:
A plane through a point with position vector $\mathbf{p}$ and parallel to two nonparallel vectors $\mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2$ has the parametric equation $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{p}+s\mathbf{v}_1+t\mathbf{v}_2$. The given direction vectors have cross product $\langle-43,-11,14\rangle\ne\mathbf0$, so they determine a plane. Substituting gives

$$
\mathbf{r}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\-3\\\sqrt2\end{bmatrix}+s\begin{bmatrix}2\\-4\\3\end{bmatrix}+t\begin{bmatrix}1\\5\\7\end{bmatrix},\qquad s,t\in\mathbb R.
$$
